bearings.paper_claim: Political DEBATE base and large are DeBERTa V3 NLI models (starting from Laurer et al. 2023 NLI checkpoints) further trained on PolNLI, 201,691 documents and 852 hypotheses. Each document is paired with a templated hypothesis and labeled entail or not entail. Full-training base hyperparameters: learning rate 2e-5 for 20 epochs (Appendix C.1). Few-shot runs used the default learning rate for 5 epochs with no tuning.
bearings.paper_location: p.2-4 (NLI framing); p.4-8 (PolNLI and training); p.12 (few-shot setup); p.25 (Appendix C.1)
bearings.system_side: finetune_debate.py starts from mlburnham/Political_DEBATE_base_v1.0 and builds three premise-hypothesis pairs per release using the template 'This text is {}.' with the labels supportive of, opposed to or critical of, and neutral toward or not about credit unions. The true label gets entailment and the other two get contradiction. Script defaults: learning rate 2e-5, 3 epochs, batch 8.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct provenance: same released checkpoint and same NLI framing. Epoch count differs: 3 in the script, 5 in the paper's few-shot runs, 20 in the paper's full training. Whether 3 epochs at lr 2e-5 suits a 552-row fine-tune is untested against the CU gold.
bearings.verifier_note: All paper numbers and framing confirmed in the text. The 20-epoch full-training setting is also relevant. The run's seed 42 and 3-epoch setting come from the vault system note (melange-stance), not from a run log.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper recommends the large model for zero-shot and most few-shot use, and the base model for simple few-shot or supervised work. On COVID threat minimization the base model largely fails zero-shot and does not match the supervised Electra classifier (MCC 0.66) in accuracy at 100 samples; the text gives no base MCC. The large model matches the classifier at 10 samples (MCC 0.67, accuracy 87 percent) and exceeds it at 25 (MCC 0.69, accuracy 88 percent). On Polistance quote tweets, Claude 3.5 scored MCC 0.29, base 0.62 and large 0.88.
bearings.system_side: Training and inference default to the base checkpoint (finetune_debate.py:32; stage5_debate.py:38). The brain actor note records that base was chosen because the machine is CPU-only, a large fine-tune takes about 3 hours with memory risk, and the plan originally named large. Zero-shot base reached 53 percent accuracy with oppose F1 0.08 on the 156-row Claude-labeled test. Fine-tuned base scored 0.796 on the 760-row gold frame and 0.571 on the adversarial frame.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies only if CU stance with sign-flip targets counts as bespoke in the paper's sense, which the oppose F1 of 0.08 suggests but does not prove. The paper reports MCC on binary tasks; the system task is 3-class. The base-versus-large gap on the adversarial frame has not been measured.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper text says the base model fails to match the supervised classifier in accuracy at 100 samples, not MCC. The MCC 0.66 belongs to the supervised classifier, so the original sentence mixed metrics. Everything else checked out, including the 53 percent and 0.08 figures and the CPU and 3-hour rationale.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper recommends short, simple hypotheses close to the training templates, and says tasks needing long or multi-condition hypotheses call for few-shot training. During training, neutral and contradiction were merged into not-entail (footnote on p.6), so neutral is not a trained positive concept.
bearings.system_side: The neutral hypothesis is the compound 'neutral toward or not about credit unions'. Inference scores the three hypotheses independently (multi_label=True) and takes the argmax, after truncating documents to 3000 characters. Training uses a 1600-character lede within a 384-token window.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Fine-tuning on 552 rows partly offsets the template mismatch. Whether splitting neutral into a not-about-CUs hypothesis plus an explicit neutral rule beats the compound hypothesis is untested. Press releases are longer than the paper's short-document zero-shot condition.
bearings.verifier_note: The footnote on neutral and contradiction merging is on p.6, not p.4. The code details (multi_label, argmax, 3000-character truncation, 1600-character lede, 384-token window) are confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper uses MCC as its primary metric, chosen for its relative robustness compared with F1 and accuracy on binary classification (p.9). It excludes GPT-4o from the benchmark because GPT-4o was used in label validation, and it discourages benchmarking OpenAI models on PolNLI for that reason (p.9-10). The paper does not say this exclusion would inflate agreement.
bearings.paper_location: p.9 (MCC choice); p.6-7 (GPT-4 and GPT-4o label validation); p.9-10 (benchmark exclusion)
bearings.system_side: The 87.2 percent accuracy, macro-F1 0.833 and kappa 0.771 are agreement with the Claude reference on the 156-row held-out test (brain actor note, 2026-06-22). Separately, live fine-tuned accuracy 0.839 with kappa 0.760 on n=87 held-out (2026-06-30). The topic note reports about 85 percent and kappa 0.76 on a member-grouped human gold. No MCC is recorded.

Do not merge the 156-row 87.2 percent figure, the n=87 0.839 figure and the about 85 percent member-grouped figure.
bearings.verifier_note: The metrics are not in the cited code lines. They come from the brain actor note, and the member-grouped label appears only in the topic note, unreconciled with the n=87 live figure. The paper's MCC rationale mentions robustness, not imbalance. The GPT-4o inflation claim is the analyst's inference. The 0.851 figure in the brain is a target, not a result.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper says NLI classifiers work best zero-shot on commonly understood concepts such as support for a person or policy. They are weaker on bespoke concepts needing specialized domain knowledge, where few-shot or supervised training is advised. This is qualitative guidance; the paper does not test a decomposition.
bearings.system_side: CU alignment is scored as a stance hop and a valence hop. The concept note reports stance 0.915 and valence 0.689 on the 400 tweet golds, measured 2026-07-04, with valence as the bottleneck. The valence registry was derived from the user's own valence judgments (11 entries; 5-fold CV compose 0.782). A hand-curated 14-entry seed exists but the curated path is an unbuilt option. Zero-shot DEBATE misses implicit policy-anti stances.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The concept note does not name DEBATE as the 0.915 stance-hop model; it refers to the stance stack. The paper supports the pattern, not the mechanism. Valence is a bespoke concept, which is the paper's stated condition for weakness.
bearings.verifier_note: The valence registry is derived from the user's golds, not curated, per the concept note. The Wall Street example sits in the actor note at line 89, not in the two-hop concept file the analyst cited. The relation stays supports, but the paper gives only qualitative support.

bearings.paper_claim: NLI zero-shot works best when labels can be derived from the text alone, without meta-knowledge about who wrote it (p.16). On quote tweets, which carry two opinions from two people, the hardest set: Claude 0.29, base 0.62, large 0.88 MCC. DeBERTa Large NLI had negative correlation with the correct labels on that set.
bearings.system_side: The planned Phase 2 branches the NLI hypothesis by speaker_source so ACU-authored rows get 'advocacy group praising or criticizing this member', then retrains. The plan is blocked on ACU-signal labels, and its gate is held-out accuracy of at least 0.851.

bearings.transfer_conditions: The meta-knowledge condition applies directly, since the paper names authorship. ACU texts about a member resemble two-voice quote tweets only by analogy; the paper gives no result for advocacy-group-about-member texts. Base-versus-large on such texts is untested.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper figures and the meta-knowledge condition confirmed. The two-voice analogy is the analyst's, not the paper's. The Phase 2 and gate lines are confirmed at 134 and 136.

bearings.paper_claim: On the COVID threat-minimization task only, the large model matches a supervised classifier at 10 samples (MCC 0.67 vs 0.66) and exceeds it at 25 (MCC 0.69). The base model, per the text, fails to match the supervised classifier's accuracy at 100 samples. The claim is confined to that bespoke task.

The vault system note reports a LinearSVC at 83.9 percent on n=87 and gives 0.757 for a transformer, which is not located in code. Fine-tuned DEBATE accuracy of 0.839 on the same n=87 ties the SVM.

The SVM-versus-transformer pair is not a DEBATE result and 0.757 is unverified. The 760-row stack is a meta-learner, not a supervised classifier alone.

related.why: Same first author. The paper defers to Burnham (2024), Stance detection: a practical guide in Political Science Research and Methods, for NLI best practice and cites its finding that larger NLI models generalize better to unseen tasks. The item is dated 2023 (arXiv 2305.01723, PSRM 2025); the paper cites 2024.

Compares fine-tuned RoBERTa with traditional ML for political-tweet stance, the transformer-versus-SVM question the system's supervised stack and DEBATE reader raise. The paper itself does not cite it.

Paul's vault cites it as the anchor for LLM position labels (GPT-4 zero-shot, 96.9 percent on keyword-prefiltered lobbying lines). DEBATE is the small open NLI alternative the system runs. Kim's task does not transfer directly.

Paul's vault cites its personality-cue result: few-shot LLM prompting 0.77 beats fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa 0.70, which beats a bag-of-words SVM 0.63. The cited line does not name GPT-4o. DEBATE is a small NLI encoder in a different slot.
Covers using LLMs to label political text, the pre-labelling step behind PolNLI (GPT-4 and GPT-4o) and the CU stance set (Claude). Its models are GPT-3 and GPT-4 on sentiment, not NLI.
Paul's vault describes it as fusing three LLM decisions by attention routing for stance on VAST, not an NLI method. It is a possible comparator for the NLI reader, not the same method.

summary_issues: summary_md says the base model could not match the supervised classifier (MCC 0.66) at 100 samples. The paper's text gives that comparison as accuracy, not MCC.

summary_md calls this the actual checkpoint behind the Melange CU press stance reader. DEBATE is one of five readers, and build_media_blend replaces its sign with the stack label, so the checkpoint is one component of the stance output, not the output itself.
summary_md says the valence-hop bottleneck matches the paper's warning about bespoke concepts. The paper does not discuss valence; this is the analyst's reading.

summary_md says both models beat the general NLI models, Llama and Claude on zero-shot MCC. The paper's text says only more performative overall; per-model MCC values are in Figure 1 and were not extracted.
summary_md and bearing 4 set the about 85 percent and kappa 0.76 figure beside the 87.2 percent figure. These are different test sets (156 rows; n=87 human gold) and should not be merged.

paul_alignment says Paul's DEBATE position cites Kim, Birkenmaier, Peng and Taherdoost, not Burnham. His stance system note does cite burnham-2023-stance-detection-practical-guide, and no Peng citation was found. The claim that he calls SVM outdated was not found in the cited note.

paul_alignment reads the system figures as the base model losing to a supervised classifier. DEBATE fine-tuned accuracy 0.839 and the SVM at 83.9 percent tie on n=87, and the 0.757 transformer figure is unverified.

The docstring in stage5_debate.py cites Burnham, Kahn, Peskoff et al., Political Analysis 2025. The paper reviewed is Burnham, Kahn, Wang and Peng, arXiv 2024. The docstring citation does not confirm the checkpoint's source; the mismatch is unresolved.
